subject.title: exec: allow-always script grants survive content changes

question: Should an allow-always grant for a concrete interpreter script delegate continuing trust to its path and arguments, or only to the exact file content approved by the operator?
rationale: Either choice changes the durable authorization contract: content pinning invalidates existing grants and increases prompts, while path trust deliberately permits later script edits to execute without re-approval.

options.title: Pin approved content
options.body: Persist and revalidate the script digest for durable grants, invalidating legacy entries that lack a binding.

options.title: Disable durable script grants
options.body: Keep one-shot approvals but remove allow-always eligibility for mutable interpreter file operands under strict-inline-eval mode.

options.title: Keep path-scoped trust
options.body: Retain current reuse semantics and explicitly document or warn that trusting a script path also trusts its future contents.

recommendation.title: Pin approved content
recommendation.body: Persist and revalidate the script digest for durable grants, invalidating legacy entries that lack a binding.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged changes most directly established reusable strict-inline-eval interpreter approval semantics and the associated regression coverage.
